attacker_input: A traditional sort key specification with a character position of UINTMAX_MAX, such as +0.18446744073709551615R.
notes: GNU Coreutils 9.7 contains the vulnerable begfield pointer arithmetic. The upstream fix identifies CWE-127, states the bug was introduced in 7.2, hardens both begfield and limfield, and adds tests/sort/sort-field-limit.sh. limfield is retained as a patched function, not promoted to a verified vulnerable location without separate evidence.

attacker_input: A crafted fixed-string pattern shorter than one eleventh of a large final input buffer that drives grep -F's memchr_kwset search pointer beyond the end pointer.
notes: Savannah's annotated v2.21 tag peels to the frozen source revision, whose released src/kwset.c contains the vulnerable bmexec_trans implementation. The upstream fix changes bmexec_trans and adds tests/kwset-abuse, explicitly naming grep 2.19 through 2.21 as affected; Savannah ancestry places the fix after v2.21 and before v2.22. NVD assigns CWE-119. Stack callers remain call-path evidence and are not promoted to vulnerable functions.

attacker_input: A local attacker able to modify a writable parent directory can substitute a filesystem object after mkdir creates the requested path but before mkdir -m changes permissions through that pathname.
notes: GNU Coreutils 5.2.1 src/mkdir.c::main creates an ordinary mkdir -m directory and then calls chmod through the pathname. Its -p path calls the historical lib/makepath.c::make_path helper, which independently creates the final directory and performs a pathname chmod when special mode bits require a post-creation change. make_dir only creates and reports state, so it is not promoted. Upstream commit 52893ffd hardens main with descriptor-based chmod_safer; the later a60cc14/76b12f0 redesign replaces the historical helper with make_dir_parents and removes temporarily permissive directory creation. Official 5.97 source still predates that redesign, while v6.0 contains the changes and the open/fchmod-capable dirchownmod implementation also present in v6.1. A later GNU reply names then-current test version 6.1 but does not establish it as the first fixed release. Debian's 6.10-1 package version is downstream evidence, not the upstream fixed version. NVD supplies only its general NVD-CWE-Other classification.
